what_it_does: This paper describes a clock oscillator—the circuit that generates the timing pulses that synchronize a chip's operations—built in a cutting-edge 3-nanometer manufacturing process. The novel contribution is that this oscillator achieves two normally conflicting goals: it produces a stable, predictable clock at 100 million cycles per second, AND it can detect when an attacker tries to disrupt the clock signal (a 'glitch' attack). Most prior designs either do one or the other. The work is motivated by security: chip initialization and defense against external clock attacks require on-chip timing circuits with built-in attack detection.
